Subject: Re: Discovery - Prompt collection & next steps

Hi Ava / Ben -

Thanks again for taking the time today - great conversation and helpful context on the invoicing edge cases you see (multi-line items, obfuscated account numbers, and regulatory redaction requirements). Per our agreement on the call, could you share a sample set of customer prompts (and a few edge-case examples) so our evaluation team can: 1) run a model-fit bench, 2) validate output redaction behavior, and 3) identify likely quality regressions for common workflows?

Quick asks:
- A CSV containing ~50-200 real anonymized prompts (one per row) that cover both typical and edge-case scenarios.
- A short mapping of sensitive fields you want redacted (column names / examples).
- Any specific output constraints (formatting, required fields, token limits).

I attached a template CSV that you can drop prompts into (acme_customer_prompts.csv) and a sample PII mapping (acme_pii_mapping.xlsx). If you prefer, you can also paste 10-15 examples directly in a reply.

Timeline: if we can get the prompts by end of day Wednesday (May 20), our evaluation team will have an initial model-fit summary and recommended model list by Friday (May 22).

Thanks - looking forward to the sample prompts.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Hi Marissa -

Thanks for the recap and template. I've attached a first pass of ~60 prompts exported from our support workflow (redacted where necessary) and a spreadsheet that maps the PII fields we want to ensure are either redacted or tokenized. A few notes:

- The dataset includes a handful of worst-case examples (internal account numbers masked with #### and free-text notes with phone numbers).
- We prefer redaction for account numbers and SSN-like patterns; names can be pseudonymized.
- For some invoices we require the AI to return a structured JSON with keys: invoice_id, line_items[], total_amount, redacted_fields[].

Attachments: acme_customer_prompts.csv, acme_pii_mapping.xlsx

Let me know if this is sufficient or if you need more examples.

Subject: Re: Discovery - Prompt collection & next steps

Hi Ava -

This is perfect, thanks for sending. Next steps from our side:

- I'll kick off a model-fit run against the prompt CSV. Our initial pass will evaluate: accuracy of extracted structured fields, false-positive/false-negative redaction rates, and token-efficiency.
- We'll produce a short model recommendation: (1) recommended baseline model for production (cost/latency tradeoff), (2) a smaller quantized candidate if you want lower-cost inference, and (3) a backup robust model for high-sensitivity/PII-heavy inputs.
- Sharing preliminary benchmark link and a HubSpot deal note once the run completes.

Dev - tagging you for the redaction guidance and to flag any potential quality-regression checks we should include in the eval (e.g., hallucinated line_items, incorrect totals). Would appreciate a short checklist you can run against the results.

Ava / Ben - do you have any hard SLOs for latency or inference cost constraints that we should consider when recommending models?

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ava Smith <ava.smith@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Turner <ben.turner@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-05-19T13:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery - Prompt collection & next steps

Thanks Marissa / Ava -

I'll run the eval and include the checklist below. A few technical notes up-front:

Checklist for prompt-set evaluation (we'll run these automatically and include metrics):
- Field extraction accuracy (precision/recall for invoice_id, total_amount, line_items count)
- Redaction fidelity: detect sensitive tokens and ensure they're replaced or masked per mapping (report FP/FN rates)
- Structural validity: produced JSON parses and conforms to required schema (keys present, correct types)
- Numeric correctness: totals should match sum(line_items[].amount) within rounding tolerance
- Hallucination rate: count of generated line_items not present in source text
- Token efficiency and average latency (p50/p95) across your prompts

Redaction guidance: please confirm whether you prefer "MASK" (replace with [REDACTED]) or "REMOVE" (omit entirely) for each field in your mapping. Our pipeline treats MASK by default for account numbers and REMOVE for SSN-like fields, but we can configure per-field.

On quality regressions: if you have an existing model or baseline outputs (even a small sample), share those so we can compute delta metrics and alert on regressions vs your baseline. If not, we'll compute absolute metrics and flag high-risk failures (e.g., missing totals, malformed JSON).

I'll begin the run as soon as we have the CSV in S3 or attached here. If you prefer secure transfer, we can share an upload link that supports client-side encryption.

-Dev
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai

Thanks Dev - this is helpful. We prefer MASK for account numbers and REMOVE for SSN-like fields.

Ben and I uploaded the CSV to the secure link you provided (sent via separate email) - filename: acme_customer_prompts.csv. We don't have baseline outputs to share, so please proceed with absolute metrics and flag high-risk failures.

One more ask: when you share the recommended model list, can you include an estimate of per-100k-token cost (hosted) and an expected p95 latency for a 512-token request? That will help our procurement team evaluate tradeoffs.

Appreciate it - looking forward to the results.

Best,
Ava
